anchors.quote: Conditionally search the finite indices from col through n-1 for the unique index produced by Python's sequential max operation with key abs. The marking predicate must reproduce the ordered fold exactly: initialize the incumbent to col, visit each later index in order, and replace the incumbent only when Python's comparison abs(rows[i][col]) > abs(rows[incumbent][col]) is true. This formulation, rather than a mathematical global-maximum predicate, must handle dynamically generated NaN or infinity values according to the original Python comparison behavior.

Encode col, candidate indices, traversal order, and the exact runtime binary64 bit patterns of rows[i][col]. Although request values are initially finite, elimination at lines 18-20 can create nonfinite intermediate entries before the later checks at lines 24-25, so the encoding and reversible operations must support finite values, signed zero, infinities, and NaNs. Exact Python-compatible abs and ordered greater-than behavior, coherent access to dynamically updated rows, reversible fold workspace, ancilla cleanup, and all loading and gate costs remain unresolved.

Measure an index and classically recompute the original ordered Python max expression on the current rows to verify it. On search failure or disagreement, use the original classical expression. Preserve the zero-pivot test, row swap, elimination order, back substitution, delayed overflow detection, exceptions, and all report construction unchanged.

This conditional plan repairs the contradicted global-maximum predicate by specifying the actual order-sensitive Python max semantics. It establishes neither implementation correctness nor practical benefit.

This is a concrete update rule, unlike a bare obligation to reproduce max. The text explicitly includes NaN/infinity rather than an all-finite guard. Translate the rule directly into ordered_scan on the checker’s absolute pivot values. A finite local pass would support this pivot-selection relation only; reversible implementation, whole-plan verification/fallback, costs and quantum execution remain unresolved.
